subject: NovusHealth: subprocessor evidence kickoff and KMS clarification
messages:
From: Elaine Greene <elaine.greene@novushealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@novushealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:12:00 +00:00
Subject: Subprocessor inventory + initial evidence request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — NovusHealth's procurement/security team kicked off our vendor review for inference providers and we need a compact evidence bundle to start the legal/security review. Can you provide the following by EOD next Thursday (2026-12-03)?

- A current subprocessor roster with roles, country of operation, and whether they process plaintext customer data (CSV preferred).
- Key pages from your latest SOC 2 report showing security control scope and third-party reliance.
- CAIQ/consensus assessment answers for cloud/inference controls (PDF).
- A simple dataflow diagram showing where customer data flows (ingest -> model runtime -> logs/metrics) and any subprocessors that have access at each hop.
- Clarify KMS integration options: do you support customer-managed KMS for hosted vs private deployments? Who holds keys for hosted customers?

Also please highlight any subprocessors engaged for telemetry/monitoring, analytics, or support that might be able to access request metadata or telemetry. If you have a secure link (Drive/SFTP) where we can pull the SIG/C-AIQ, include it.

Appreciate a compact cover note summarizing the answers so our legal & infosec folks can triage.

Best,
Elaine
Senior Vendor Risk Manager
NovusHealth

--

- Hosted customers: by default we use Redwood-managed KMS for token sealing and ephemeral runtime encryption. We offer customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own) for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we can enter an agreement for CMEK on a per-account basis but note there are regional constraints (EU CMEK requires additional setup).
- Subprocessors that may see metadata/telemetry: our metrics vendor (ObservIQ) receives anonymized metrics and aggregated telemetry; the support provider can access request IDs and troubleshooting traces but never full request payloads for hosted customers unless customer-approved debug trace is enabled. Details in roster.
- Delivery plan: PDF + CSV attached to this email for initial review. Full SIG questionnaire is large — we will upload the completed SIG/Lite to a secure share and send the link within 24 hours.

Open items for Novus to confirm:
1) Do you prefer SFTP or secure Drive link for retrieval?
2) If CMEK is a requirement for hosted, please confirm regional KMS key residency requirements.

We can also schedule a 30-minute walkthrough this week if the security team wants to go over the dataflow and KMS options.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Third-Party Risk
Redwood Inference

Hi Elaine — quick technical responses below (inline):

> 1) For hosted customers where Redwood-managed KMS is used, who is the KMS provider and where are the master keys provisioned (region/custody)?
- Hosted (default): Redwood-managed KMS uses AWS KMS in the region where the tenant is provisioned. For EU-region hosted tenants we provision keys in eu-west-1 by default. Master keys are under Redwood account but access is restricted and auditable; for customers that require control we offer CMEK (customer-managed keys) on Dedicated/Private and an enterprise option for hosted where keys can be provisioned in a customer-owned AWS account under a cross-account model (requires DPA addendum).

> 2) For the monitoring/telemetry subprocessors: does any vendor receive request payloads or raw prompts in any environment (hosted, dedicated, private)?
- No subprocessor receives raw customer request payloads in hosted or dedicated environments. For Private (customer-managed) deployments, telemetry vendors run in-customer VPCs only and do not receive raw request payloads outside the customer's network. Support engineers may request a redacted debug trace (customer opt-in) which we provide via secure share.

> 3) What is your default log retention for request traces and how quickly can logs be purged on customer request?
- Default retention: 30 days for request traces by default in hosted. We offer configurable retention down to 0 days for Dedicated/Private. Purge SLA: upon approved request we can remove traces from active storage within 72 hours and cascade removals from backups per our retention policy (audit action logged).

> 4) export of model parameters or artifacts?
- Model artifacts are stored in our artifact store. Exporting model parameters is a supported operation only for model owners and never performed by telemetry/support subprocessors. Fine-tuning jobs that require vendor-managed compute are subject to contract controls and are currently only performed in Dedicated or Private configurations under customer authorization.

Hope this helps — happy to hop on a call with your engineers.

Jonas Weber
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
